# CUT THE FLOW — Full Documentation for LLMs

> CUT THE FLOW is a browser-based non-linear video editor (NLE) that runs entirely on the client
> side. This document is the technical and functional reference for AI systems that need to
> understand, describe or operate the application.

**Version**: 3.10.1 (September 2026)
**Author**: Simon Dupont (Zigmoon)
**Website**: https://cuttheflow.com
**Releases**: https://app.zigmoon.com/release.html

---

## 1. Overview

CUT THE FLOW is a 100 % client-side video editing application. There is no server, no upload and
no account: media files are read locally by the browser and never leave the device. It supports
multi-track timeline editing with five clip types: **video, audio, image, text overlay** and
**colour block**.

Typical workflow: import media by drag & drop → arrange clips on the timeline → cut, trim, fade,
apply effects and colour grading → optionally ask the AI assistant to perform edits → export to
MP4, WebM or MP3.

---

## 2. Architecture

### File structure

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Single entry point: all UI markup (toolbar, media library, preview, timeline, modals) |
| `js/app.js` | Core application, one class: `CutTheFlow` (exposed as `window.app`) |
| `js/frame-source.js` | `CTFFrameSource` — frame-accurate image extraction for the export engines |
| `js/webcodecs-export.js` | MP4 engine: WebCodecs H.264 + AAC, muxed with MP4Box |
| `js/webm-webcodecs-export.js` | WebM engine: WebCodecs VP9 + Opus, inline EBML muxer |
| `js/mp3-export.js` | MP3 engine: audio-only export through LAME |
| `js/canvas-export.js` | Last-resort real-time engine (MediaRecorder), non-deterministic |
| `js/export-safeguards.js` | Capability detection and memory guards for export |
| `js/ctf-advanced.js` | Waveforms, transitions, subtitles, performance index |
| `js/i18n.js` | French / English strings |
| `css/style.css` | Entire dark-theme stylesheet |
| `service-worker.js` | Offline app-shell caching |
| `manifest.json` | PWA manifest |
| `tools/regression/` | Permanent export test bench (Chrome + ffmpeg, no npm dependency) |
| `vendor/` | JSZip 3.10.1, MP4Box.js 0.5.2 (patched), lamejs 1.2.1 (LAME 3.100) |

No build step, no bundler. Every JavaScript file is loaded by a `<script>` tag in `index.html`
and listed in the service worker's `APP_SHELL`.

### Core class `CutTheFlow`

Manages the media library (import, thumbnails, proxy generation), the timeline (tracks, clips,
playhead, zoom, snapping), the preview, colour grading, the clip effects, the three export
engines, the AI assistant, the undo/redo history, the auto-save (IndexedDB, every 30 s) and the
project files.

---

## 3. Timeline model

### Tracks

- Stacked vertically; **track 0 (`VIDEO 1`, top of the UI) is the foreground**, drawn last.
- Default tracks: `VIDEO 1`, `VIDEO 2`, `VIDEO 3`, `AUDIO 1`, `AUDIO 2`.
- Properties: `id`, `name`, `muted`, `solo`, `volume` (0-100), `clips[]`.

### Clips

- Placed by `startTime` + `duration`, in seconds.
- `sourceStart` = offset into the original media (for trimmed clips); `sourceDuration` = original
  duration.
- Common properties: `trackIndex`, `trackId`, fades (`fadeIn`, `fadeOut`), effects, animation
  preset.

### Clip types

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `video` | References a media item. `videoScale`, `videoPosX`, `videoPosY`, optional `transition`, optional subtitles |
| `audio` | References a media item. Can be created by unlinking a video's audio |
| `image` | Still frame for the clip duration, with the same spatial transform as video |
| `text` | Canvas-rendered text: `content`, `style` (font, size, colour, optional shadow), `posX`/`posY` in percent |
| `block` | Coloured rectangle: `color`, `width`/`height`, `posX`/`posY` (percent), `opacity` |

---

## 4. Export engines

The export dialog offers **exactly three choices — MP4, WebM, MP3** — with no mode tabs and no
engine picker: the engine follows from the format.

### MP4 — WebCodecs H.264 + AAC (offline, deterministic)

- `VideoEncoder` (H.264) + `AudioEncoder` (AAC-LC, 48 kHz stereo, 192 kbps).
- Muxed to MP4 by MP4Box.js, including a hand-written `esds` box for the audio track.
- Every frame is decoded **exactly at its timeline position** before being encoded, so the result
  is identical on every machine — only the elapsed time varies.
- If the browser cannot encode H.264, the export falls back to WebM **and says so**.

### WebM — WebCodecs VP9 + Opus (offline, deterministic)

- `VideoEncoder` (VP9) + `AudioEncoder` (Opus, 48 kHz stereo, 128 kbps).
- Muxed by an inline EBML/WebM muxer that uses the encoder's **real `OpusHead`** (correct
  `preSkip`), so the audio is not shifted.
- Smaller files at equal quality; the recommended format for long montages.
- Falls back to the real-time engine only if VP9 is unavailable, with an explicit warning.

### MP3 — audio only, LAME 3.100

- The timeline audio is decoded, mixed (track volume, fades, unlinked audio, time bounds) and
  encoded with `lamejs` (LAME) at 48 kHz stereo, 192 kbps.
- The MPEG-1 Layer III encoder delay is compensated, so MP3 landmarks fall at the **same instants**
  as in the MP4 export.

### Frame-accurate extraction (`js/frame-source.js`)

Each video clip gets its own `<video>` element, left **paused**. For every output frame the engine
seeks to the **middle** of the wanted frame and waits for `seeked`. Reason: seeking exactly on a
frame boundary makes Chrome return the wrong frame one time out of three (measured), which
produced duplicated and skipped images — the cause of the stutter and the audio/video drift that
affected earlier builds.

Per-clip statistics are reported at the end of every export (`seeks`, `duplicates`, `skips`,
`errAvg`, `errMax`, `failures`); the reference values are **0 duplicates, 0 skips, 0.0 ms**.

### Real-time fallback (`js/canvas-export.js`)

Last-resort MediaRecorder path for browsers without WebCodecs. It is **not** deterministic
(measured drift from −2.4 % to +11.6 % on long montages) and the user is always warned before it
is used.

### Export guards

- If the hardware encoder stalls, the export fails after **20 seconds** with an explicit message
  instead of waiting forever.
- An export started in a **background tab** is frozen by the browser: the app warns the user to
  keep the tab visible.
- The chosen export format is remembered in `localStorage` and inside the project file.

---

## 5. Quality assurance — the permanent regression bench

`tools/regression/` drives a real Chrome through the DevTools protocol (no npm dependency) and
verifies the produced files with ffmpeg. It builds a **13-second, 5-track control edit** — two
videos with audio landmarks (440/880 Hz and 1 200 Hz), one photo, a title, a shape and two audio
tracks — exports it in the three formats, saves the project as `.ctf` and `.json`, reloads the
page, reopens both files, then checks everything.

Reference results (latest run: **29 checks out of 29**):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Frames | 390 / 390 (MP4 and WebM) |
| Audio landmarks | exact instants, **0 ms** offset |
| Sync difference WebM / MP3 vs MP4 | **0 ms** |
| Frame extraction | 300 seeks, **0 duplicates, 0 skips, 0.0 ms error** |
| Black frames at the cuts | none |
| Fidelity against the source | **0 differing frames** (max deviation 1/255) |
| Layer order, text, shape | present only inside their time range |
| Project round trip | 5 tracks / 7 clips / 5 media, export format restored |

Usage:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/regression/make-media.ps1   # once
node tools/regression/montage.cjs            # full run
node tools/regression/montage.cjs --quick    # MP4 export only
```

---

## 6. AI assistant

### Providers — order of display, **DeepSeek first and default**

| Provider | Models offered |
|---|---|
| **DeepSeek** (default) | `deepseek-flash` = **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, `deepseek-v4-pro` |
| **OpenRouter** | no-cost tier models (`:free` suffix) and paid ones |
| **Groq** | no-cost tier models, very fast inference |
| **OpenAI** | GPT-5.1, GPT-5, GPT-5 Mini, GPT-4.1, o3, o4-mini |
| **Anthropic** | Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| **Google** | Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite |

### Integration

- Direct browser-to-API calls; the provider must allow CORS.
- **One API key per provider**, stored in `localStorage` under `ctf_ai_apikey_<provider>`
  (an older global `ctf_ai_apikey` is still read as a fallback for DeepSeek).
- Conversation history is kept (maximum 20 messages).
- DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq and OpenAI share one OpenAI-compatible code path, which retries
  without the optional parameters when the API answers 400 or 422.
- Responses are parsed defensively: ```json fences, surrounding prose and trailing commas are
  tolerated.

### Action schema

The assistant answers with JSON: `{ "explanation": "...", "actions": [ ... ] }`.

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `ADD_CLIP` | Add media from the library to a track |
| `DELETE_CLIP` | Remove a clip |
| `MOVE_CLIP` | Reposition a clip (time / track) |
| `TRIM_CLIP` | Change a clip's in / out points |
| `SPLIT_CLIP` | Cut a clip at a given time |
| `RIPPLE_DELETE` | Delete a clip and close the gap |
| `SET_CLIP_PROPERTY` | Set a clip property (name, content, colour, opacity, dimensions) |
| `SET_CLIP_STYLE` | Update a text clip's styling |
| `UNLINK_AUDIO` | Extract a video's audio onto its own track |
| `ADD_TEXT` | Create a text overlay |
| `ADD_BLOCK` | Create a colour block |
| `ADD_TRACK` / `DELETE_TRACK` | Track management |
| `MUTE_TRACK` / `SOLO_TRACK` / `SET_VOLUME` / `RENAME_TRACK` | Track controls |
| `SET_COLOR_GRADING` | Global colour grading |
| `APPLY_FILTER_PRESET` | Named presets (cinema, vintage, noir, sepia, …) |
| `SEEK` / `MARK_IN` / `MARK_OUT` / `SET_ZOOM` | Navigation |

---

## 7. Keyboard shortcuts

**Playback**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Space` / `K` | Play / Pause |
| `J` | Rewind 1 s |
| `L` | Forward 1 s |
| `←` / `→` | Step back / forward one frame |
| `Home` / `End` | Go to start / end |

**Editing**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `C` | Cut at the playhead |
| `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` | Copy / paste a clip |
| `U` | Unlink audio from video |
| `Delete` | Delete the selected clip |
| `Shift+Delete` | Ripple delete |
| `I` / `O` | Mark in / mark out |

**Text and overlays**

| Gesture | Action |
|---|---|
| Double-click | Edit a text clip |
| Drag | Move a text or colour block in the preview |
| Drag a corner handle | Resize video / image (aspect ratio preserved) |

**View and project**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `+` / `-` | Zoom in / out |
| `Ctrl+P` | Toggle the properties panel |
| `Ctrl+S` | Save the project |
| `Ctrl+Z` | Undo |
| `Ctrl+Y` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | Redo |
| `Escape` | Deselect / close a panel |

---

## 8. Projects, auto-save and publishing

- **`.ctf`** — JSZip archive containing `project.json` plus the media blobs: a self-contained
  project.
- **`.json`** — the project description only; media stay referenced by URL.
- Both formats store `appVersion` and `selectedFormat`, so a reopened project comes back with the
  same export format. Projects saved by older versions still open.
- `Infinity` is serialised as `"__INF__"` and restored on load (used by image clips, whose source
  duration is infinite).
- An auto-save runs every 30 seconds into IndexedDB (`ctf_autosave`, key `latest`) and is offered
  for restoration at start-up.
- Publishing to IPFS through Pinata is available; the JWT is kept in `sessionStorage` only.

---

## 9. Offline use (PWA)

`service-worker.js` pre-caches the app shell (`CACHE_NAME`, versioned per release) and
`manifest.json` makes the app installable. The shell list must stay synchronised with the
`?v=` cache-busters used in `index.html`; a release changes both.

---

## 10. Interface conventions

- Dark theme, **true black** backgrounds (`#000`) for the toolbar, panels, timeline and track
  lanes; track separation lines are deliberately faint (`#131317`) and the time grid uses 3 %
  white.
- Track buttons **M** (mute) and **S** (solo) are outlined; only their active states are filled
  (red for mute, orange for solo).
- Timeline, ruler, zoom, properties panel and media library are keyboard reachable; focus rings
  are visible and `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected.

---

## 11. Known limits and behaviour worth knowing

- **The real-time engine is not deterministic.** If WebCodecs is unavailable, the app falls back
  to MediaRecorder and warns the user; the output length can drift on long montages.
- **Background tabs freeze the export**: browsers throttle hidden tabs. Keep the tab visible.
- **Vendor libraries are loaded locally** (`vendor/`) so the app works offline; do not replace
  them with CDN links without updating the service worker.
- **The MP4 muxer is a local build of MP4Box.js with a patch** (the `first_dts` fix, without which
  every track is shifted by one frame). Do not restore the unpatched file.
- Long montages are best exported to **WebM (VP9 + Opus)**, which is the most exact on very long
  timelines; MP4 is recommended for compatibility.
